note: The geography channel's formats, tiers from research/families.json (17 Nov 2026). demand: the niche hits each rests on.

formats.name: What if: a world that changed
formats.emotion: wonder and play: imagine it with me
formats.hook: The what-if question is the first line, over the map it changes: 'What if the entire world became one country?'
formats.beats: the question -> what changes first (a figure the viewer knows) -> a countdown or a race of consequences, one place each -> the twist nobody expects -> the payoff that answers the title -> a last line that loops to the first frame

demand.title: What If the Entire World Became One Country
Can Countries Roll Down a Hill

formats.name: Why a place is shaped or placed like that
formats.emotion: the satisfaction of an odd map finally making sense
formats.hook: Name the place and ask why in the first line, the odd shape on screen: 'Why does Gambia sit inside Senegal?'
formats.beats: the place and the question -> its shape put on a map the viewer knows, for scale -> the first cause (a river, mountains, a coast) shown on the map -> the second cause (a treaty, a war, a trade) -> the payoff: the one fact that explains it -> loop

demand.title: Why Chile Is So Long & Narrow

formats.name: Rankings and comparisons on a map
formats.hook: The ranking's surprise in the first line: 'Only 14 of 170 countries make it to the bottom of the hill.'
formats.beats: the rule of the ranking -> the famous ones fail early -> an underdog rises -> the viewer's own region -> the winner -> loop

demand.title: Every Country's Longest and Shortest Ruling Leader

formats.name: A place and what makes it rich or poor
formats.hook: A place and a paradox: 'This desert country has no rivers, yet it's one of the richest on Earth.'
formats.beats: the place and the paradox -> the resource or route, shown on the map -> who controls it -> what it changed -> the payoff -> loop
